alexandria.description: Execute one or more catalogued provider tools instead of scraping a URL. Cannot be combined with `url`, `formats`, or other scrape options (400); the only allowed sibling keys are `timeout`, `origin`, and `integration`. Use the `x-request-id` request header as a client-chosen idempotency key (1 to 128 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, `-`) — it is echoed back, and a completed request with the same key replays its original response and `scrape_id` instead of re-executing. To browse the catalogue and read tool contracts for free, call Find Tools: set `provider` to `firecrawl`, `capability` to `find-tools`, and `options` to a `FindToolsOptions` object. The result `data` is a `FindToolsData` page.

domainTools.description: When true on an ordinary URL scrape, `data.tools` lists tool contracts matched to the scraped page's domain (same `DiscoveredTool` shape as search). Requires the team's Alexandria access to be enabled and no zero data retention (403 otherwise). Free.

findTools.summary: Find Tools: browse the Alexandria catalogue (free)
findTools.description: Calls the `firecrawl/find-tools` capability. It lists the tools of the `particle` provider and does not execute them. Follow an item's `next` call, or the page's `next` call, with another `alexandria` request.

post.summary: Crawl multiple URLs based on options

url.description: The base URL to start crawling from

prompt.description: A prompt to use to generate the crawler options (all the parameters below) from natural language. Explicitly set parameters will override the generated equivalents.

excludePaths.description: URL pathname regex patterns that exclude matching URLs from the crawl. For example, if you set "excludePaths": ["blog/.*"] for the base URL firecrawl.dev, any results matching that pattern will be excluded, such as https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-launch-week-1-recap. Patterns use Rust regex (RE2-style) syntax: look-around and backreferences are not supported, and a pattern that does not compile is rejected with a 400. Each field accepts at most 1000 patterns of at most 2000 characters each, and includePaths and excludePaths together may contain at most 1000 patterns and 100,000 characters in total. For keyword-style filtering, send one short pattern per term rather than combining terms into a single long alternation.

includePaths.description: URL pathname regex patterns that include matching URLs in the crawl. Only the paths that match the specified patterns will be included in the response. Note: the starting URL is also checked against these patterns — if it does not match, the crawl may return 0 pages. For example, if you set "includePaths": ["blog/.*"] for the base URL firecrawl.dev/blog, only pages under /blog/ will be included in the results, such as https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-launch-week-1-recap. Patterns use Rust regex (RE2-style) syntax: look-around and backreferences are not supported, and a pattern that does not compile is rejected with a 400. Each field accepts at most 1000 patterns of at most 2000 characters each, and includePaths and excludePaths together may contain at most 1000 patterns and 100,000 characters in total. For keyword-style filtering, send one short pattern per term rather than combining terms into a single long alternation.

maxDiscoveryDepth.description: Maximum depth to crawl based on discovery order. The root site and sitemapped pages has a discovery depth of 0. For example, if you set it to 1, and you set `sitemap: 'skip'`, you will only crawl the entered URL and all URLs that are linked on that page.

sitemap.description: Sitemap mode when crawling. If you set it to 'skip', the crawler will ignore the website sitemap and only crawl the entered URL and discover pages from there onwards. If you set it to 'only', the crawler will only crawl URLs from the sitemap (plus the start URL) and will not discover links from HTML.

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Do not re-scrape the same path with different (or none) query parameters

regexOnFullURL.description: When true, includePaths and excludePaths regex patterns are matched against the full URL (including query parameters) instead of just the URL pathname. Useful when you need to filter URLs based on query strings.

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl. Default limit is 10000.

crawlEntireDomain.description:
Allows the crawler to follow internal links to sibling or parent URLs, not just child paths.

false: Only crawls deeper (child) URLs.
→ e.g. /features/feature-1 → /features/feature-1/tips ✅
→ Won't follow /pricing or / ❌

true: Crawls any internal links, including siblings and parents.
→ e.g. /features/feature-1 → /pricing, /, etc. ✅

Use true for broader internal coverage beyond nested paths.

allowExternalLinks.description: Allows the crawler to follow links to external websites. External links are followed one hop (the links found on those external pages are not crawled). Links pointing to an external site's homepage (a root URL with no path) are skipped and reported in Get Crawl Errors with the code EXTERNAL_LINK; redirects to an external homepage are skipped for the same reason.

allowSubdomains.description: Allows the crawler to follow links to subdomains of the main domain.

ignoreRobotsTxt.description: Ignore the website's robots.txt rules. Enterprise only — contact support@firecrawl.com to enable.

robotsUserAgent.description: Custom User-Agent string for robots.txt evaluation. When set, robots.txt is fetched with this User-Agent and allow/disallow rules are matched against it instead of the default. Enterprise only — contact support@firecrawl.com to enable.

delay.description: Delay in seconds between scrapes. This helps respect website rate limits. Setting this forces concurrency to 1.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum number of concurrent scrapes. This parameter allows you to set a concurrency limit for this crawl. If not specified, the crawl adheres to your team's concurrency limit.

url.description: The URL to send the webhook to. This will trigger for crawl started (crawl.started), every page crawled (crawl.page) and when the crawl is completed (crawl.completed or crawl.failed). The response will be the same as the `/scrape` endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to send to the webhook URL.

metadata.description: Custom metadata that will be included in all webhook payloads for this crawl

events.description: Type of events that should be sent to the webhook URL. (default: all)

zeroDataRetention.description: If true, this will enable zero data retention for this crawl. To enable this feature, please contact help@firecrawl.dev

post.summary: Start an agent task for agentic data extraction

urls.description: Optional list of URLs to constrain the agent to

maxCredits.description: Maximum credits to spend on this agent task. Defaults to 2500 if not set. Values above 2,500 are always billed as paid requests.

strictConstrainToURLs.description: If true, agent will only visit URLs provided in the urls array

model.description: The model to use for the agent task. spark-2 is the default and the model every run executes on. The Spark 1 model names remain accepted for backwards compatibility but are deprecated and route to spark-2.

effort.description: Reasoning budget for the agent task. Every run executes on spark-2, so effort can be sent with or without model.

webhook.description: A webhook specification object. Subscribes to agent lifecycle events (agent.started, agent.action, agent.completed, agent.failed, agent.cancelled).

url.description: The URL to send webhook events to.

headers.description: Headers to send to the webhook URL.

metadata.description: Custom metadata that will be included in all webhook payloads for this agent job.

events.description: The events to send to the webhook URL. Defaults to all events.

threadId.description: Continue an existing thread: pass the `threadId` an earlier run returned, and this request runs as that thread's next turn. Omitted `urls`, `schema`, `effort`, `mode` and `exchange` settings carry over from the previous turn. Omit `threadId` to start a new thread.

mode.description: `extract` returns the complete structured result in `data` every turn. `chat` lets a follow-up that asks for no new data get a short reply in `message` instead of a re-run. `exchange.requireApproval` needs `chat` on the same request. Omitted on a follow-up turn keeps the thread's mode.

exchange.description: Let the agent call your team's [Alexandria](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/alexandria) data providers during the run. Without this object the run uses the web only (a follow-up turn inherits the previous turn's settings). See [Use your connected Alexandria tools](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/agent#use-your-connected-alexandria-tools).

enabled.description: Let the agent call Alexandria providers. Defaults to `true` once `exchange` is sent; send `false` to turn providers off for a turn of a thread.

toolkits.description: Pin up to 5 providers by slug, for example `["apollo"]`. The agent then uses only those. Empty or omitted means every provider your team can use.

maxCalls.description: Most provider calls the agent may make in this turn.

requireApproval.description: Before any paid provider call, end the turn with a `pendingApproval` of kind `calls` that you approve or decline on the next turn. Requires `mode: "chat"` on the same request, including on a follow-up.

approve.description: Answer yes to the `pendingApproval` the previous turn of this thread ended on. Needs `threadId`.

callIds.description: Run only these calls from the approval. Defaults to all of them. Ignored on a `terms` approval.

always.description: Stop asking for approval for the rest of the thread. Ignored on a `terms` approval.

decline.description: Answer no to the `pendingApproval` the previous turn of this thread ended on. Needs `threadId`. A declined `terms` offer keeps its providers out of the rest of the thread.

onTermsRequired.description: What to do when a provider the agent would use needs data terms your team has not accepted. Such providers are never called. `skip` answers with accepted providers and lists the others in `exchange.skippedProviders`; `ask` also ends the turn with a `terms` `pendingApproval` and `exchange.requiresAction`. Omitted on a follow-up turn keeps the previous turn's value. See [Data providers that need terms](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/agent#data-providers-that-need-terms).

threadId.description: The thread this run belongs to. Pass it as `threadId` to continue the thread.

threadTurn.description: This run's turn in the thread, starting at 1.

numPages.description: For PDF inputs, the number of pages parsed (capped by the parsers maxPages option).

totalPages.description: For PDF inputs, the document's true page count before any maxPages capping. Omitted when it cannot be determined; a totalPages greater than numPages indicates the result was truncated.

error.description: The error message of the page

concurrencyLimited.description: Whether this scrape was throttled due to team concurrency limits

concurrencyQueueDurationMs.description: Time in milliseconds the request waited in the concurrency queue. Only present when concurrencyLimited is true.

invalidURLs.description: If ignoreInvalidURLs is true, this is an array containing the invalid URLs that were specified in the request. If there were no invalid URLs, this will be an empty array. If ignoreInvalidURLs is false, this field will be undefined.

title.description: The title of the page, if available.

description.description: A description of the page, if available.

invalidURLs.description: If ignoreInvalidURLs is true, this is an array containing the invalid URLs that were specified in the request. If there were no invalid URLs, this will be an empty array. If ignoreInvalidURLs is false, this field will be undefined.

status.description: The current status of the extract job

tokensUsed.description: The number of tokens used by the extract job. Only available if the job is completed.

SearchFeedbackRequest.description: For 'good', include valuableSources. For 'partial', include valuableSources or missingContent. For 'bad', include missingContent or querySuggestions.

question.description: Question or issue for the support agent to diagnose.

rationale.description: Optional context about what the end user is trying to accomplish.

fixParameters.description: Machine-readable API parameters that may fix the issue.

validation.description: Validation result when the support agent tested or attempted a fix.

feedback.description: Present when the support agent is blocked or needs more information.

durationMs.description: Total support-agent execution time in milliseconds.

answer.description: Concise answer grounded in Firecrawl documentation.

durationMs.description: Total docs-search execution time in milliseconds.

error.description: Support proxy or upstream error code.

RedactPIIEntity.description: Public PII entity buckets supported by Firecrawl redaction.

mode.description: Redaction strategy. `accurate` is model-only and optimized for precision, `aggressive` increases recall with additional heuristics, and `fast` uses heuristics without the model call.

entities.description: Restrict redaction to these entity buckets. If omitted, all supported entities are redacted.

replaceStyle.description: `tag` replaces spans with placeholders like `<EMAIL>`, `mask` replaces characters with `*`, and `remove` deletes the span text.

semantic.description: Semantic score from the intent search.

seedOverlap.description: Number of distinct seeds connected to this candidate.

paperId.description: Canonical paper id, or web:<url> for SERP-discovered display results.

primaryId.description: Preferred cite/fetch id such as arxiv:<id>, pmid:<id>, pmcid:<id>, or doi:<id>.

text.description: In-body passage text. May include markdown tables.

score.description: Dense similarity score for the passage.

type.description: Result kind.

title.description: Frequently absent on `doc` results, where the source page carries no usable title. Fall back to `url`.

passages.description: Matched passages in markdown, so tables and code blocks survive.

coverage.description: Outcome for each result type. Check this when an expected result type is missing: `skipped` means your `types` value did not ask for that type, while `degraded` or `unavailable` means the gap came from the index or from a filter, not from the query. A repository filter is one such cause — see [how the repository filters scope a search](/api-reference/endpoint/developer-search#how-the-repository-filters-scope-a-search).

reranked.description: Whether the ranked list went through the reranking stage.

repos.description: Present only when `repos` was sent. Echoes each slug with whether it is indexed, plus a per-type breakdown under `types`.

types.description: Which result types are indexed for this repository: `issue`, `pullRequest`, and `readme`.

sources.description: Present only when `sources` was sent. Reports each id exactly as requested along with whether it is indexed. `indexed: true` means the source has a published generation, so documentation evidence from it may appear; `indexed: false` means nothing from that id can match, which distinguishes an id that is not in the index from a query that simply found nothing.

description.description: Matched snippet from the source document.

allOf.description: Submit feedback for a v2 job. Include at least one substantive signal such as issues, note, valuableSources, missingContent, querySuggestions, url, or pageNumbers.

metadata.description: Small endpoint-specific metadata object. Must be 8KB or smaller; do not include full endpoint results.

ThreatProtectionOverride.title: Threat Protection Override
ThreatProtectionOverride.description: Per-request [Threat Protection](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/threat-protection) override. Fields you provide replace the corresponding fields of your organization's policy for this request only; omitted fields keep their organization-level values. Requires Threat Protection to be enabled for your team (enterprise feature) — otherwise the request is rejected with a 403. If your organization has disabled request overrides, any request that includes this object is rejected with a 403. If Threat Protection is enforced for your team, `mode` may not be set to `off`.

mode.description: URL scanning mode for this request. `normal` checks URLs against Google Web Risk (+2 credits per URL scanned).

riskScoreThreshold.description: Normalized risk score (0–100) at or above which a classifier verdict blocks the URL. Lower is stricter.

blacklist.description: Domains to always block, as plain domains (`example.com`) or wildcard globs (`*.example.com`). No protocol, path, or port.

whitelist.description: Domains to always allow, as plain domains or wildcard globs. Wins over every other rule.

blockedTlds.description: Top-level domains to block outright, lowercase without the leading dot (e.g. `zip`).

failurePolicy.description: What to do when the classifier can't be reached: `closed` blocks the request, `open` allows it.

AgentPendingApproval.description: What the turn stopped to ask. Answer it on the next turn of the thread with `exchange.approve` or `exchange.decline`.

kind.description: `calls`: paid provider calls held back by `requireApproval`. `terms`: providers whose data terms need accepting (`onTermsRequired: "ask"`). Absent on items written before terms offers existed, which are `calls`.

reason.description: Why the agent wants to make these calls.

calls.description: The paid calls waiting for approval. Empty on a `terms` approval.

id.description: Pass in `exchange.approve.callIds` to approve only some calls.

input.description: The options the call would run with.

more.description: Further inputs the same call would run with.

creditsEstimate.description: Estimated credits, or null when unknown.

terms.description: On a `terms` approval, the providers whose terms need accepting.

digest.description: Null when the catalog published no digest; `terms/show` returns it.

url.description: Where a person accepts the terms in the dashboard.

resolution.description: Null until a later turn answers the approval.

AgentExchangeSummary.description: What the run did with Alexandria. `toolkits` and `requireApproval` are what the run resolved to after thread inheritance.

toolkits.description: Pinned providers. Empty or absent means every provider the team can use.

paidCalls.description: Paid provider calls the run made.

creditsUsed.description: Credits the provider calls used, or null when unknown.

skippedProviders.description: Providers that would have helped but need data terms your team has not accepted. Any `onTermsRequired` mode.

adds.description: What the provider would have added.

termsUrl.description: Where a person accepts the terms in the dashboard.

requiresAction.description: `onTermsRequired: "ask"` only, when a terms offer ended the turn: the calls to view and accept each provider's terms. Nothing here runs for you, and `terms/accept` must only be called after your user explicitly agrees.

approvalId.description: The `terms` `pendingApproval` to answer once the terms are accepted.

digest.description: Null when the catalog published no digest; `terms/show` returns it.

show.description: The `terms/show` call, as `{ provider, capability, options }` for `/v2/scrape` `alexandria`.

accept.description: The `terms/accept` call, as `{ provider, capability, options }` for `/v2/scrape` `alexandria`.
